sec.title: 2. Executive Summary
sec.p: This document sets out an estimated financial budget and cost proposal for the design, development, launch, and three-year maintenance of the An Tobar website, in response to the RFT issued by COGG. The RFT sets a fixed ceiling of €75,000, VAT inclusive, for a 3-year contract comprising 1 year of development and 2 years of maintenance, with a target launch date of August 2027.

Given the scale of the required platform — a bilingual (Irish/English), fully editable, filter-driven educational resource site with distinct primary and post-primary experiences — and the tightness of the €75,000 ceiling, this proposal is built around a lean delivery model: a small Ireland-based project liaison layer supported by a nearshore/offshore delivery team engaged on a contractor day-rate basis, rather than a full Irish-based salaried team. This approach is disclosed transparently in Section 5 and Section 10.
Key headline figures (all VAT inclusive unless stated):
●​Maximum RFT budget: €75,000.00 (VAT inclusive)
●​Estimated net project cost (excl. VAT): €60,975.61
●​Estimated VAT at the 23% standard rate: €14,024.39
●​Total estimated contract value (incl. VAT): €75,000.00 — exactly at the RFT ceiling
●​Remaining budget headroom: €0.00 beyond the contingency reserves already built into each year (see Section 13)

The proposal is assessed as commercially feasible only under the lean, nearshore-supported delivery model described herein, and only if the assumptions in Section 18 (particularly around content volume, integrations, and COGG-provided assets) hold. Section 20 sets out this feasibility assessment in full.

sec.title: 4. Key Financial Assumptions
sec.p: This proposal is built on the following high-level financial assumptions. Detailed scope assumptions are set out in Section 18.

●​The RFT budget of €75,000 is VAT inclusive; the applicable Irish VAT rate for the services described (web design, software development, and digital consulting) is the standard rate of 23%, per Irish Revenue rules (see Section 5).

●​Delivery is modelled using a small Ireland-based liaison/PM presence combined with a nearshore/offshore development, design, and QA team engaged as contractors, rather than a full Irish salaried team, in order to fit within the ceiling. This is a commercial assumption, not an RFT requirement — see Section 10.
●​All personnel costs are modelled as contractor/freelancer day rates (not gross salary + employer PRSI), except where explicitly marked as an Irish employee cost.
●​Costs are apportioned across Year 1 (development), Year 2 (maintenance) and Year 3 (maintenance) in line with the RFT's 1+2 year structure.
●​A contingency reserve of approximately 10% is built into each year's budget (see Section 13).
●​Figures are estimates for tender planning purposes and are not a quotation, an approved COGG budget, or a guarantee of actual cost.

sec.title: 5.2 Commercial (non-statutory) market assumptions
sec.p: The following are market estimates, not legal requirements, and are clearly distinguished as such:

●​Nearshore/offshore contractor day rates for development, design and QA roles are estimated at €150–€250 per day, reflecting typical EU/nearshore digital agency rates for a public-sector education project of this scale, not Irish full-time salaried equivalents.
●​The Ireland-based project liaison/PM day rate is estimated at €450–€500 per day, reflecting typical Irish senior digital-project-management contractor rates.
●​An Irish accessibility/compliance specialist day rate is estimated at €350–€400 per day.

●​For reference only (not used in this cost model, since no Irish employees are assumed): a full-time Irish mid-level developer salary is commonly quoted in the €45,000–€65,000 gross range, to which employer PRSI (Section 5.1) and other on-costs would be added — this is materially higher than the budget ceiling would support for a dedicated Irish team across 3 years.

sec.title: 5.3 Employee vs contractor cost model — this proposal
sec.p: This proposal uses a contractor/day-rate model throughout, not an employee salary model, except for the small Ireland-based liaison role which may be engaged either as a contractor or via an existing employer of record. No gross-salary-plus-employer-PRSI calculation is used elsewhere in this budget, and the figures below should not be read as implying Irish full-time employment for the nearshore roles.

sec.title: 8. Infrastructure & Third-Party Costs
sec.p: Infrastructure is modelled on lean, cloud-based hosting appropriate to a resource website of this scale, split between one-time setup and annual recurring costs.

sec.p: Testing is concentrated in Year 1, ahead of go-live, with light-touch annual regression checks folded into the maintenance retainers in Years 2 and 3 (Sections 11–12) rather than budgeted as a separate line.

sec.title: 10. Launch & Deployment Budget
sec.p: Launch and deployment costs are folded into the Year 1 Infrastructure and Development lines above rather than budgeted separately, given the scale of the project. They comprise:
●​Production environment configuration and CI/CD setup
●​Domain/DNS cut-over and SSL/TLS configuration
●​Backup configuration and go-live monitoring
●​Go-live support during the August 2027 launch window

Because the €75,000 ceiling cannot support a large Irish-based full-time delivery team across 3 years, the delivery model assumed for these activities — and for development generally — is a lean core team: a small Ireland-based PM/liaison for governance, stakeholder engagement, and NDA/accessibility sign-off, supported by a nearshore/offshore team for design, build, and QA, using cloud-based infrastructure and reusable components rather than custom-built infrastructure from scratch.

Where an offshore/nearshore delivery model is used, this proposal assumes: (a) all client-facing engagement, requirements sign-off, and NDA/accessibility liaison is handled by the Ireland-based liaison; (b) data is hosted within the EU/EEA to support GDPR compliance; (c) security and support requirements are coordinated through the Ireland-based liaison, with defined response-time expectations agreed with COGG during onboarding; and (d) COGG retains full back-end/admin access regardless of where development is performed, per the RFT's Section 6 requirement.

sec.title: 15. VAT Calculation
sec.p: The RFT states the €75,000 budget is VAT inclusive. Web design, software development, and digital-consulting services supplied in Ireland are, in the ordinary case, subject to the Irish standard VAT rate of 23%. This proposal therefore treats the full contract value as standard-rated.

tr.td: B. Net project budget excluding VAT

sec.p: VAT treatment is not automatically uniform across every supplier or cost line:
●​Services supplied by an Irish-VAT-registered contractor are charged Irish VAT at 23% in the normal way.

●​Where nearshore/offshore contractors are engaged from outside Ireland, business-to-business supplies of services to an Irish-established client are generally subject to the EU/Irish reverse-charge mechanism (the Irish recipient self-accounts for VAT) rather than the supplier charging foreign VAT — this should be confirmed with an Irish tax adviser for the specific supplier arrangement used.

●​Certain infrastructure/SaaS subscriptions (e.g. non-EU cloud providers) may also fall under reverse-charge or place-of-supply rules rather than the flat 23% assumption used here for budgeting simplicity.

sec.title: 18. Assumptions
sec.p: This budget is materially dependent on the following assumptions. Any of these proving incorrect would require the budget to be revisited via change control.

●​Scope: a single bilingual (Irish/English) resource website with primary and post-primary sections, editable tabs/buttons/filters, and a CMS, as described in RFT Appendix 1 — not a native mobile app or a separate LMS.

●​Page/section volume: broadly in line with the homepage, primary, and secondary section structures shown in the RFT (in the order of 15–25 distinct page templates/layouts, not hundreds of unique page designs).

●​Initial resource volume: COGG provides an initial, bounded set of resources (documents, videos, worksheets) for launch content population; large-scale ongoing content creation is excluded (Section 19).
●​Content migration: limited migration of existing COGG materials; large-scale historical content migration is treated as a chargeable addition.
●​Integrations: no third-party LMS, payment, or SSO integrations beyond basic authentication/admin access are assumed.
●​Traffic/users: a school-resource-site traffic profile (not a high-traffic consumer platform), consistent with standard, cost-efficient cloud hosting.
●​Hosting: cloud-based hosting within the EU/EEA to support GDPR compliance.
●​Support hours/SLA: standard business-hours support during Years 2–3; no 24/7 support is assumed (Section 19).

●​Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA is targeted in design and build, with annual NDA inspection preparation included; this proposal does not guarantee NDA certification, which rests with COGG's inspection process.

●​Security & data protection: baseline GDPR-aware security controls appropriate to a public-sector education site handling data relating to minors; a full independent security audit/penetration test is not included unless requested.
●​Third-party services: limited to the infrastructure items costed in Section 8; no paid premium third-party APIs are assumed beyond this.
●​Branding: COGG provides final colour scheme, logo, and branding guidance (RFT notes colours are 'to be confirmed').
●​Approvals: COGG provides timely review and sign-off at each milestone; delays in approval may affect the schedule but not, in themselves, the budget.
●​Change requests: any request outside the RFT's stated scope is treated as a chargeable change request, priced and approved separately.
●​Delivery model: a nearshore/offshore-supported delivery team is used to remain within budget; this is a commercial assumption, not an RFT requirement, and is disclosed in Section 10.

sec.title: 19. Exclusions
sec.p: The following are not included in this budget unless explicitly required by the RFT and subsequently agreed and costed as a change request:
●​Major scope changes or new features outside the approved requirements
●​Large-scale content creation or extensive historical content migration
●​Paid third-party APIs or premium software licences beyond the allowance in Section 8
●​Major integrations not specified in the RFT (e.g. LMS platforms, payment systems, SSO with school systems)
●​Hardware
●​Travel, unless specifically required and agreed in advance
●​24/7 support (standard business-hours support only)
●​Major redesigns beyond the initial design system
●​Additional applications, including a native mobile app
●​Large-scale marketing, search engine marketing, or continuous content creation
●​Independent third-party security audits or penetration testing (baseline security controls only are included)

sec.title: 20. Budget Feasibility Assessment

tr.td: D. Estimated Project Cost (net, incl. built-in contingency)
F. Contingency reserved within D (not additive)

sec.p: Conclusion: the proposal is exactly at budget. It reconciles precisely to the RFT's €75,000 VAT-inclusive ceiling, with a contingency reserve of approximately 9.6% of net project cost already embedded within each year's figures rather than sitting on top of the ceiling.

This result is only achievable under the lean, nearshore-supported delivery model described in Sections 5 and 10. A conventional Irish full-time salaried delivery team, at typical Irish gross-salary-plus-employer-PRSI cost levels (Section 5.2), would materially exceed the €75,000 ceiling across a 3-year, 1+2 year contract of this scope. Tenderers should treat this as a genuine commercial constraint of the RFT, not an artefact of this estimate.

Because the model is exactly at budget with no headroom beyond the embedded contingency, any of the assumptions in Section 18 proving materially incorrect — particularly around content volume, integrations, or additional accessibility/security requirements — would require either a reduction in scope, a change-controlled increase to the contract value, or a re-negotiation with COGG, rather than absorption within this budget.

sec.title: 21. Final Financial Summary
sec.p: Conclusion: the proposed financial model is commercially feasible for a 3-year Irish contract of this scope only under the lean, nearshore-supported delivery model set out in this proposal, and only if the scope assumptions in Section 18 hold. It leaves no additional headroom beyond the contingency already built into each year, so disciplined change control will be essential to keeping the project within the RFT's €75,000 ceiling.

This estimated financial model has been structured around the RFT's stated maximum budget of €75,000, VAT inclusive, for a 3-year contract consisting of 1 year of development and 2 years of maintenance, with a target website launch in August 2027.
